justification: A pairs its honeycomb image with the Origin section on A4, so text and image share the page. B puts the same image alone on B3 with a large empty lower half, and pushes the Origin heading down B4, leaving a blank top. A also includes a table of contents (A2). B uses hanging section headings that sit outdented from the body text, which reads less cohesive.

A sets text continuously on well-filled pages and marks History with a strong navy band, so the sections read as a clear structure. B uses a pleasant serif with clear numbered headings, but it leaves large gaps. B2 ends with a third of the page empty, and B5 holds only a short paragraph before a near-blank page. These make B's pacing uneven, and it runs six pages against A's five.

A sets the body in a serif text face with comfortable leading and margins, so long passages read well. Its headings are numbered and clearly stepped. A does waste most of A5 on a few lines and an orphaned image-markdown fragment. B is tighter and runs to 4 pages. Its dark section band on B2 and its header bars add structure. However, B's light sans body at a wide measure is denser and harder to read on B3 and B4. B2 also has the 'Precursors' band jammed near the page foot, leaving only three lines below it. Both designs show the broken image text. On balance, A's text quality wins.

B's serif body at a comfortable measure, with clear numbered headings and generous leading, reads more comfortably than A's dense sans-serif text with tight justification and frequent hyphenation. A's navy header band and section banner add structure, but the banner sits awkwardly at the foot of A2, with the section's text spilling onto the next page. B starts Precursors cleanly on B3. Its main drawback is the near-empty final page B5, which still carries the broken image markup, as A4 does.

A uses a serif body with numbered headings, which gives a clear hierarchy and comfortable reading. But it leaves page A5 nearly empty, with only a short paragraph before the image page, and A2 ends with a large gap. B flows the text continuously across B2–B4 with no stranded page. It adds a strong History band on B2 that anchors the section, and it finishes in five pages with even fill. B's wide sans text column is slightly denser, but its overall rhythm and balance are better.

A flows continuously: the honeycomb image shares its page with the section opening (A4) and pages fill evenly. B strands the honeycomb image on a mostly empty page (B4). It inserts a full divider page for chapter 2 with a sidebar (B5) that breaks the flow. It also leaves large blank bottoms (B7, B8), and its running header misleadingly labels the image page as Etymology. B's numbered headings are a plus, but the wasted space and choppy pacing outweigh them.

A pairs a serif body with sans headings and uses drop caps that mark each section, giving the text a more bookish, readable texture. B sets dense sans text in tight justified blocks under heavy header and footer bands, which makes the pages feel crowded. B's History band is strong, and A leaves page 5 mostly empty, but A's typography and section entry points read better overall.

A mixes inconsistent styles: headings hang outside the text column, lead paragraphs switch to larger type, and drop caps appear, all of which make the rhythm feel uneven. It also leaves large empty areas on A3, A4 and A6. B keeps one consistent body style with numbered headings and fills its pages evenly. Its header and footer bands give a clean frame (B3, B4, B5). Both designs show the same raw markdown image error.

A is tighter and more consistent: running header bands, a clear section band for Precursors, and steady text flow across four pages. B has a half-empty page B2 and a near-empty final page B5. Its inconsistent indents and large lead paragraph on B3 make the rhythm feel uneven. Both share the broken image markup.

A uses a consistent serif body with bold sans numbered headings, giving clear hierarchy and steady rhythm. B's body text is small and dense, and its oversized lead paragraphs after each light-weight heading make the text size jump. B's main headings are thin and less distinct, and its subheads are inconsistent. Both show the same raw image-markdown leak and similar photo placement. A's header and footer bands add structure, while B's thin rules are cleaner but plainer.

A uses an elegant Garamond-like serif, but its oversized lead paragraph under Precursors (A3) disrupts the hierarchy. B has numbered sans headings with running section headers (B3, B4) and slightly larger, more open body text, which make it easier to navigate and read. Both carry the same broken image markup on the last page (A5, B5).

A keeps one consistent text style, dark section bands and running headers and footers, and fills its pages evenly. B switches between ragged lead paragraphs, justified body text and drop caps. It leaves large blank areas at the top of B4 and B6 and at the bottom of B3. Its hanging headings sit awkwardly outside the text column. Both designs show the same raw markdown image error.

A sets body text in a serif face with generous leading and a larger lead-in paragraph. A also uses ruled section heads, so it reads more comfortably. B is denser, with a tight sans body. Its section band on B2 is a heavy dark block, and the running header bands add visual weight. B is more compact, and A leaves a mostly empty page on A5. Both show the raw image markdown. A's readability edge outweighs this.

A keeps one consistent text block, numbered headings and steady paragraph spacing, framed by navy header and footer bands. B mixes large lead paragraphs with small justified body text, and adds drop caps with ragged wraps. Its headings hang out into the margin. Its pages break unevenly, leaving large voids on B3, B4 and B6, so the rhythm feels disjointed. Both carry the same raw image-markdown glitch.

A pairs a humanist serif body with Montserrat heads, giving warm, readable text, and its sections flow on quiet pages. B's dense sans body and heavy dark header and footer bands on every page feel cramped. B's mid-document section divider (B4) is mostly empty and breaks the flow, and B7 is left largely blank. A has its own gaps, including the large lead-in space and lead paragraph on A4, but it reads more calmly overall.

Both designs share the same content and the same broken image markdown on the last page. A sets its classic serif in a tighter, more refined text block and uses a consistent top rule band on every page. B uses wide letterspacing and heavy justification gaps, and its h1 hangs outside the indented body, which looks misaligned (B3). B's running heads are useful, but its looser body type and uneven indentation make it read less cleanly than A.

B adds a table of contents, numbered headings, and a section divider page, which give clearer navigation and hierarchy. Its header and footer bands frame each page consistently. A has an odd hanging heading indent, with headings outdented past the text column, and an oversized lead paragraph on A4. B has a heavy divider page on B5, and B4 is mostly empty space. Even so, B reads more coherently overall.

B sets the history in a refined serif that suits the subject, with comfortable margins and quiet running feet. A's heavy navy header and footer bands and its filled History band feel heavy. A's sans text is also more tightly set and has more hyphenated breaks. Both share the same structure and image placement. A's History band gives a stronger section cue, but B reads more calmly overall.

A pairs a serif body with a sans heading, uses larger lead paragraphs and drop caps, and opens each major section on a fresh page. That gives a more refined, book-like reading experience, though it leaves some pages with large empty areas (A4, A6). B is denser and more uniform. Its heavy dark header and footer bands and its filled section bars feel corporate. Long justified sans text in B also shows rivers and hyphenation strain (B4, B5). Both reproduce the broken image markdown. Overall, A reads more comfortably.

A pairs a sans heading face with a serif body at a comfortable measure. Its numbered headings stand out clearly, and running headers show the current section (A3, A4). B sets the body at a longer measure, about 95+ characters per line (B2, B4), which is harder to read. B's "Precursors" heading is set light and is barely stronger than the oversized lead paragraph beneath it (B3), which muddles the hierarchy. Both designs share the broken image-markdown leftover on the last page (A5, B5).

A runs to five pages with a nearly empty final page (A5) that holds only two lines and a broken image link. It also leaves a large void at the bottom of A2. B fits the same content into four well-filled pages, adds running headers with section names, and gives Precursors a clear header band (B2). A's larger lead-in paragraph on A3 gives it a slight hierarchy edge, and its serif text reads well. Still, B's page fill and rhythm are stronger.

B uses a refined serif with comfortable leading, and its rule-plus-heading sections and lead paragraphs give a calmer, bookish rhythm. A's heavy navy header/footer bands and filled heading bars are strong but crowd the page, and its dense sans text with frequent hyphenation reads tighter. Both carry the same raw markdown artifact (A5, B5). B's page fill is somewhat more even, while A5 ends with a large empty area.

B adds a table of contents (B2) and numbered headings at every level (B5–B8), which makes the structure clearer than A's unnumbered headings. B's serif body text is more comfortable to read at length than A's condensed sans (A5, A6). A gets a small imagery edge because its second photo is visible (A8). Both designs leave half-empty pages (A7, B8) and use identical bands.

A adds a TOC, heavy header and footer bands, and a striking chapter divider (A5). The divider wastes a full page, and A's pages leave big empty bottoms (A4, A7, A8). B runs more continuously with fuller pages and cleaner running footers. It closes with a well-placed second image (B7), so it reads more smoothly. B4's oversized lead paragraph is a minor inconsistency.

A sets the text in a refined serif with a generous measure and fills its pages evenly, so the article runs in 5 pages with no stranded content. B leaves large gaps: B2 has a big empty bottom, and B5 holds only a short paragraph before mostly blank space. B's heavy header and footer bands with running section titles help navigation, and its numbered headings are clear. Still, the uneven page fill and denser justified text with wide word gaps weaken B overall.

B flows more compactly. Its 7 pages have no near-empty pages, while A7 is mostly blank. B also avoids A's full-page section divider (A4), whose large divider panel feels heavy for a short document. Its serif body with hanging headings reads as elegant, and its quiet folios replace A's heavy navy header and footer bars. B's one flaw is the oversized lead paragraph on B4, but overall its pacing is better.

A sets the body in a refined serif with generous margins and a light top rule, which suits a historical essay and reads calmly. B uses a sans body with wider measure and heavy dark header and footer bands on every page. Its filled History band is emphatic but visually heavy, and the dense justified sans text creates rivers on B2 and B3. The image pages are comparable.

A runs as a consistent, densely set flow: one serif family, tidy justified columns, headings aligned to the text block and a steady rhythm. B's headings hang left of the body column, which looks misaligned. B also adds drop caps inconsistently, mixing justified and ragged paragraphs. It leaves large voids, with a half-empty page after the image and big top gaps on B4 and B6, so the page rhythm is choppy. Both share the raw markdown image glitch.

A pairs a geometric sans for headings with a refined serif body, uses drop caps and a rule-led History heading, and keeps the margins quiet, so it reads as a polished book. B's heavy dark header and footer bands on every page add clutter and feel template-like, and its plainer numbered headings carry less character. A's drop caps break the paragraph rag a little and its pages are as sparse as B's, but A's typographic finish wins overall.

A strands the honeycomb photo alone on a mostly blank page (A3) and leaves a large empty top band on A4, creating broken rhythm and wasted space. A's bold sans headings with hanging indents give clearer hierarchy, but its section headings outdent past the text column awkwardly. B flows text continuously, places the image with its section (B4), adds a contents page (B2), and keeps pages evenly filled.

Design A uses an elegant serif, but its section openings use an odd enlarged lead paragraph that reads like a pull quote. This blurs the hierarchy, and the H1s are light and thin, weaker than the bold H2s. Design B gives clear, numbered bold sans headings with a consistent hierarchy. Its running header and footer bands show the current section and the page count. Its body text is larger and evenly set. Both carry the same broken image markdown, but B's pages are fuller and more evenly balanced.

A sets clean sans text under a dark header band with running section titles and a solid Precursors banner, so the hierarchy is clear. It fits the document in four well-filled pages. B's serif is pleasant, but its Precursors heading is weak and set at an odd larger body size. B also leaves half of B2 empty and spills two lines plus stray markdown onto a near-blank B5, so its page balance and rhythm are poor. Both show the broken image markdown.

B keeps one consistent text block with numbered headings, running headers carrying section names, and page X of 5 footers, which gives the pages a steady, orderly rhythm. A's Precursors lead paragraph uses a larger, differently indented style that sits awkwardly against the body text below it (A3). A's footers show inconsistent section labels, and A has no headers. A's typeface is slightly more refined. Both end with the same broken image-markup line on the last page.

A sets body text in a serif with comfortable leading and gives each section a numbered heading, which reads calmly. Its pages are evenly filled and the heading and image placement is consistent (A3, A4). B's banded H1 headings are bolder, but its light sans body text sits on dense, wide lines (B2, B4). B's last page also ends with a large empty area (B5). Both designs show the same raw image-markdown glitch (A5, B5).

A keeps a consistent serif text block, with even justification and a steady flow of pages. B is inconsistent. Its body text switches between justified and ragged-right after the drop caps (B2–B4). The History heading hangs outside the text margin (B2). B5 holds a short orphan paragraph followed by a mostly empty page before the image (B5, B6). B's drop caps and sans headings add some visual interest, but the inconsistency and wasted space outweigh them.

A strands the honeycomb photo alone on a mostly empty page (A3) and leaves the Apis page two-thirds blank (A7). Its divider page arrives after the content it introduces (A4). B flows continuously: the photo shares its page with the section opener (B4), and pages fill evenly (B5, B6, B7). B also adds a contents page (B2). A's sans type and header bands are crisp, but B's pacing and balance are clearly better.

A has section headings that hang out past the left text margin, inconsistent body styles (ragged-right drop-cap sections mixed with justified text), and large dead space where sections break pages (A3, A4, A6). B flows continuously, with consistent justified Garamond-style text, aligned headings and steady rhythm (B2–B5). Both show the same broken image markdown.

B flows continuously, with a consistent serif face and justified text, and it fills its pages evenly. A mixes ragged drop-cap paragraphs with justified ones and has wide letterspacing. A also leaves page A5 mostly empty after a few lines, and its History heading hangs outside the text margin. A's drop caps add some character, but B reads more smoothly.

Both designs share the same structure, image and page breaks. A sets the text consistently in one serif with numbered headings and dark header and footer bands. B adds drop caps whose paragraphs switch to ragged, differently tracked text (B2–B4), which is inconsistent beside its justified paragraphs. B's wide letter-spacing also makes the body look loose. A reads more evenly.

A sets the text in a refined serif with generous margins and quiet rule-based section heads, so the pages read calmly. Its oversized lead paragraphs are an oddity. B uses heavy navy header and footer bands plus filled heading bars. On every page these feel busy, and they compete with the dense sans text, which has looser justification gaps (B5). Both share the same image and the same broken markdown artifact.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body set in a comfortable measure and generous leading, which reads more easily than B's tight, wide lines of small serif text. A's sans headings with a rule (A3, A4) stand out more clearly than B's light 'Precursors' heading (B3). B's top rule bands add some polish. Both designs leave the broken image markdown on page 5 (A5, B5).

A breaks pages early, leaving large gaps: A2 and A4 have big empty bottoms, and A5 holds only a short paragraph on an otherwise blank page. It runs to six pages. B flows its text continuously across pages B2–B4, with even page fills, and finishes in five pages. A's numbered sans headings are somewhat clearer. B's rule-separated History heading is a bit light, but its subheads still read well. B's quieter header and footer bands are also less heavy than A's dark bars.

B's serif body text is more comfortable for long reading, and its numbered headings give a clear outline. Its pages fill evenly, while A5 leaves nearly half the page empty after the last section. A's dark heading bands are bold and consistent but feel heavy. Both designs show the same raw markdown image string on A5 and B5.

A holds one consistent text measure with clean running headers and numbered headings. B's Precursors intro on B3 is set in a larger font on a narrower indent that doesn't match the body text. B also splits a sentence across B4 and B5 and leaves a large empty area at the bottom of B3. Both designs show the same broken image markdown.

A has a table of contents and numbered headings (1, 2.1, 2.4.1) whose level is clear at a glance. Its serif body text reads comfortably. B drops the TOC and numbering, which flattens the hierarchy, and its light sans body is slightly harder to read. B does use its pages more efficiently and ends with a strong image page. A leaves large gaps, though, such as the lone image on A4.

A flows continuously, keeping the honeycomb image with its section and adding a useful table of contents (A2, A4). B leaves the honeycomb stranded on a mostly empty page (B3). It then inserts a divider page for only the second section (B4), and leaves half of B7 blank before pushing the last subsection to B8. That creates erratic pacing and large wasted areas. B's heavy header and footer bands and dense justified sans text also read less comfortably than A's serif text.

Design A sets the text densely and consistently across pages. Its header and footer bands frame each page well, and it fits the content into 5 pages. Design B has some strengths: an elegant serif, drop caps and a clean rule-line heading. But its drop-cap paragraphs switch to ragged text, which makes the texture inconsistent. Page B2 ends with a large gap, and page B5 is mostly empty with a short stub of text, which weakens the page rhythm.

A strands its honeycomb image alone on a mostly empty page (A4) and inserts a near-empty chapter-divider page (A5). Several pages then end with large blank areas (A7, A8). B flows its text continuously, places the image with the following section (B4) and fills its pages evenly through to the second photo (B7). A's numbered headings and running header bands give clearer navigation, but B's pacing and use of space are much better.
